scope: Corollary 2.8 (Gaussian weights and polynomial dilations) of the manuscript “Almost-everywhere regularity of stationary integral varifolds” (preprints/Almost-everywhere-regularity-of-stationary-integral-varifolds-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 346 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f12bd8f9ace9a350), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 13-14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Define Gs(y) = (2πs2 )−m/2 exp(−|y|2 /(2s2 )) 13 and fix a center x. On the region |y − x| ≤ Rs, cover the base by balls of radii comparable to s/(1 + |y − x|/s), with fixed enlarged balls having bounded overlap. Suppose each enlarged ball meets the hypotheses of Theorem 2.5 with the same propagated integer Q. Then ∫ |y−x|≤Rs Gs(y − x) d|M|(y) ≤ C ∫ |y−x|≤(R+C)s Gs(y − x) d(D + Λ)(y). (2.23) The constant is independent of R. The part outside the indicated region is retained as a tail error. For the configuration conclusion, fix one exceptional proportion δcmp > 0 smaller than the fixed comparison-overlap proportions. If, in addition, on all admissible dilations 1 ≤ t ≤ R∗ one has (ts)−m τ(Bcts(x)) ≤ CtJ d, (2.24) with CtJ d ≤ d0(δcmp) throughout this range and the same integer propagated, then configurations matched from the scale s have moment and support estimates on a dilation t equal to those in Theorem 2.7, with an additional fixed power of t. Gaussian integrals of these estimates have constants depending on J and the fixed moment order, once the tail beyond R∗ is accounted for.
